title: A bounded precession model supports HD 303514 eclipse loss near 2030 but dilution can delay the exit to 2032
abstract: We test whether the HD 303514 eclipse-loss forecast depends on a linear drift. We fit 15 published ASAS-3 and TESS depths with a circular twin binary and constant precession, with a bound on the projected orbital normal. At the adopted dilution, a delta chi-square tolerance of 3.84 gives a first-exit grid range of 2029.7-2031.0. The best curved fit has chi-square 20.66. An independent search for models with no finite interval of eclipse loss gives 33.82. Separate band dilutions from 0.4 to 1.0 give a best curved fit of 14.35 and a best no-loss fit of 30.79. Two seeds agree, including a search for shorter period aliases. Equal-band dilution tests allow exits as late as 2032.3 but have worse fits. The nodal period remains poorly constrained. These are conditional fit comparisons, not calibrated confidence limits or a companion detection. Stellar geometry, uncertain dilution and correlated depth errors limit the result. Code, aggregate input, hashes, tables and static figures are included.
